subject: Disputed invoice INV-202705: request for per-prefix usage export and jurisdiction attribution
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@storify.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice #INV-202705 - unexpected usage spike

Hi Evelyn,

We're seeing a sizable overage on invoice INV-202705 (attached) — roughly 2.4M tokens over our expected baseline. Our engineering team ran a cursory check and suspects token attribution may include requests from a legacy integration using the org-level API key (we rotate keys, but that key was provisioned to a partner). Can you please: 

- Provide a per-prefix / per-customer_tag usage export for 2027-04-28 through 2027-05-07 (CSV).
- Include request_id, timestamp, model, token_in, token_out, and any prefix/customer_id fields used for attribution.
- Confirm whether any EU VAT reclassification applied to these lines (Storify is US-headquartered but we have EU customers).

We appreciate a quick turnaround — we need this for our internal controller and to decide whether to withhold payment on the disputed portion.

Attachments: INV-202705.pdf (invoice PDF)

Thanks,
Alex Cho
Head of Finance | Storify, Inc.
alex.cho@storify.io
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice #INV-202705 - unexpected usage spike

Team — forwarding Storify's ask (see attached invoice). They want a per-prefix export and confirmation on VAT treatment. Priority: high — they're considering withholding payment.

Action items:
- Markus: can you run the usage export with group_by=prefix, include request_id and customer_tag and filter 2027-04-28T00:00:00 through 2027-05-07T23:59:59?
- Ben: will you pull a small sample (1000 lines) first and check for any obvious replay/duplicate request_id patterns?
- Monica: can you flag any potential EU VAT reclassification if attribution shows EU-origin traffic?

Please keep me looped — I'll coordinate with Storify and ask for more detail if needed.

Forwarded attachments: INV-202705.pdf

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Finance | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Invoice #INV-202705 - unexpected usage spike

On it. I will run a full export but recommend the following to triage quickly: 

1) Run usage-export with these columns: timestamp, request_id, api_key_id, prefix, customer_tag, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, region, http_user_agent. Filter window 2027-04-28..2027-05-07.
2) Produce a sample of unique(request_id) counts vs total rows to detect duplicates/replays.
3) If api_key_id shows the same org-level key behind multiple customer_tag values, that hints at attribution leakage.
4) If we find many identical request_id with different timestamps but same payload, that suggests replay.

If evidence supports a misattribution, propose provisional credit while we finish audit export. How much? need to see magnitude but we can do pro-rata.

I'll queue the export now (may take ~2 hours).

-Markus
VP, Billing & Entitlements | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Invoice #INV-202705 - unexpected usage spike

Attached is a 1k-line sample from the export (usage-export-sample.csv). Quick summary from the sample: 

- ~18% of rows have repeated request_id values (same request_id appears 2-5x across window).
- Several repeated request_id entries have identical tokens_in/tokens_out and only differ by timestamp; timestamps cluster around 2027-05-02T03:20:00-03:30:00 UTC.
- api_key_id for repeated groups is the org-level key we expect Storify used for their partner integration. customer_tag sometimes maps to other Storify sub-orgs.

Prelim root cause: likely a replay loop from their integration retries (partner webhook duplicated events) causing duplicated server-side processing.

Recommendation: offer a provisional credit for the duplicated token portion (we can compute from the full export). For speed, propose applying a 60% provisional credit on the disputed line items while we finish the full audit export and validate exact duplicates.

Attachments: usage-export-sample.csv

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@storify.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Invoice #INV-202705 - unexpected usage spike

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Ben and team.

We ran our side of the integration and can confirm our partner's webhook attempted retries during the same window — we think those were replays and are happy to cooperate. Two requests: 

1) Can you share an ETA for the full export and the proposed provisional credit amount?
2) We'll sign a standard reconciliation acknowledgement (DocuSign) to accept adjusted billing if the audit matches. Link to our controller's PO: PO-5521.

We appreciate the provisional credit proposal; that will help clear our internal hold while you finish the audit.

Alex Cho
Head of Finance | Storify, Inc.
alex.cho@storify.io

Date: 2027-05-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice #INV-202705 - unexpected usage spike — provisional credit applied

Alex — quick update and next steps.

1) Full export is complete and attached (redwood-usage-export-20270428-0507.csv). We ran duplicate request_id detection across the window and estimate ~2,176,400 tokens attributable to duplicated requests.
2) Per our provisional policy and the magnitude here, we've applied a provisional credit of USD 3,600 to invoice INV-202705 pending final reconciliation. The provisional credit will appear as line CR-202705-17 on your account; it's applied so you can release the payment hold.
3) Next: we'll reconcile definitively within 5 business days. If our final audit reduces the duplicated count, we'll invoice the delta; if it increases, we'll notify you before applying any further adjustments.

I've attached a provisional-credit-note.pdf and the full export. Please sign the DocuSign reconciliation if you'd like the expedited path (link in prior message). Also attaching HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9241.

Attachments: redwood-usage-export-20270428-0507.csv, provisional-credit-note.pdf

If you want a short sync (15m) to walk through the CSV, happy to set up with our CS/Tech Ops.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
